arguments.summary: A credential compromise occurred on host WS-FIN-AP01 after a phishing email triggered execution of encoded PowerShell from Outlook, leading to a malicious DLL being loaded via rundll32. The payload established C2 communication to 198.51.100.23:443. The initial access vector was traced to external IP 185.220.101.42, which previously conducted network scanning against internal asset WS-IT-101 (10.0.2.15). Although sandbox analysis returned 'clean', behavioral telemetry and IOCs confirm malicious activity. Full host scan identified a low-severity PUP, but core threat was not detected by AV.

User CORP\jsmith launched outlook.exe on WS-FIN-AP01.
Encoded PowerShell executed as child of Outlook (T1566.001).
rundll32.exe loaded unsigned DLL from Temp directory (T1218.011).
Incident response initiated; EDR and SIEM data collected.
Full EPP scan of WS-FIN-AP01 completed; detected PUP.Optional.BrowserHelper (low severity).

arguments.rule_content:
title: Suspicious PowerShell Execution from Outlook
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
  event_id: 4688
conditions:
  - NewProcessName|endswith: '\\powershell.exe'
  - ParentProcessName|endswith: '\\outlook.exe'
  - CommandLine|contains: '-enc'
  - CommandLine|contains: 'hidden'
level: high
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
description: Detects encoded and hidden PowerShell launched directly from Outlook, commonly seen in phishing payloads.

arguments.summary: A critical lateral movement incident was detected originating from external IP 45.33.32.156, which conducted a network scan against host 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101) on 2026-04-08. The scan was initially blocked by IDS, but subsequent lateral movement occurred after valid credentials (CORP\helpdesk) were used from the compromised host to access the 10.0.12.0/24 subnet. No malicious payloads were found on the initial host, but authentication logs indicate successful access to a sensitive subnet. Asset inventory and firewall policies could not be retrieved due to access restrictions, limiting visibility into segmentation effectiveness.

timeline.description: External IP 45.33.32.156 performed a SYN scan on host 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101), detected and logged by IDS with signature 'ET SCAN Nmap SYN Scan'.

Successful authentication from 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101) to 10.0.1.1 using CORP\helpdesk credentials.
Multiple successful authentications observed from 10.0.2.15 into the 10.0.12.0/24 subnet, indicating lateral movement.
Incident investigation initiated after delayed detection. No containment actions were approved during Admin phase.
